title: The Secret else Clause Hiding in Python's for Loop
description:
Python's for loops can have an else clause -- and it does something most developers never expect. It only fires if the loop finishes without ever hitting break, which makes it perfect for "did I actually find it?" search patterns. Full lesson on Python control flow, loops, and the match statement is linked below.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/python-mastery-path/level-1/03-control-flow/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Every Python for loop can have a secret else clause -- and most developers have never used it.
This loop searches numbers 2 through 20 for the first multiple of 7. If it finds one, it prints it and breaks.
Run it, and you get 7 -- the loop broke early, so that else block never even runs.
Here's the twist: that else isn't tied to the if. It's tied to the loop itself. It only fires if the loop finishes normally, without ever hitting break -- perfect for search patterns.

display.heading: for / else
display.subheading: else runs only when the loop completes WITHOUT break
